7. Populations and index events

David Sarrat González

Source: vignettes/book-07-populations.Rmd
book-07-populations.Rmd

What you will learn

Choose who enters a study, define episodes and observation coverage, reuse a cohort, identify new users and sample controls at case time.

This chapter uses the 24-person synthetic questionnaire test fixture described in Getting started.

You need: the packages and the matching practice connection described in Before you start. Run its sections in order. Each chapter starts from a fresh practice connection; all the outputs below come from real dsOMOP and dsOMOPClient 2.10.4 calls. The numbers describe teaching data, not clinical findings.

Start this chapter

Start a fresh R session in the book-work directory created in Getting started. Run this setup first:

library(dsOMOPClient)
source("tools/book/display.R")
source("tools/book/fixture.R")
practice <- book_fixture()
conns <- practice$conns
names(conns)
#> [1] "site"

The site connection is ready. This chapter creates its temporary questionnaire fixture locally.

Start with an index event

A population specifies who contributes rows. An index selects an event date for each study episode. Here a person’s first visit starts one episode.

visits <- omop_event("visit_occurrence")
visitors <- omop_population("visitors", index = omop_index(visits, select = "first"))
class(visitors)
#> [1] "omop_population" "list"

People without visits are absent. The default episode end is the end of the covering observation period. select = "all" would keep recurrent visit episodes.

Release membership as a private table 

visit_members <- omop_recipe(populations = list(visitors),
  outputs = omop_output("members", rows = "visitors", format = "membership"))
stopifnot(recipe_explain(visit_members, conns = conns)$selected == "v2")
print(recipe_execute(visit_members, out = c(members = "D_members"), conns = conns))
#>     members 
#> "D_members"

Membership includes pseudonymous keys and episode dates. Inspect its schema, not its patient rows:

dsBaseClient::ds.colnames("D_members", datasources = conns)
#> $site
#> [1] "row_id"            "cohort_row_id"     "person_id"         "cohort_start_date"
#> [5] "cohort_end_date"   "index_source"

The default date fields are offsets from the index. Several episodes can belong to the same person; a row count is not necessarily a person count.

Require an eligible visit

A criterion is an inclusion test. These criteria require an inpatient record on the index day and at least 365 days of observation before it.

inpatient <- omop_event("visit_occurrence", concepts = 9201L)
eligible <- omop_population("eligible",
  index = omop_index(visits, select = "first_eligible"),
  filters = list(omop_observed(before = 365),
    omop_has(inpatient, window = omop_window(0, 0))))
class(eligible)
#> [1] "omop_population" "list"

first_eligible tests the complete criterion tree at each candidate, then selects the earliest passing visit. first selects a person’s first visit before testing; it would not advance to a later visit when that first one fails. Combine alternatives with omop_any() and joint requirements with omop_all(). Only TRUE survives; an unknown criterion is not evidence of eligibility.

eligible_recipe <- omop_recipe(populations = list(eligible),
  variables = list(visits = omop_count("visit_occurrence", before = Inf)),
  outputs = omop_output("people", rows = "eligible", format = "wide"))
stopifnot(recipe_explain(eligible_recipe, conns = conns)$selected == "v2")
print(recipe_execute(eligible_recipe, out = c(people = "D_eligible"), conns = conns))
#>       people 
#> "D_eligible"

The count includes visits through the chosen index day.

dsBaseClient::ds.summary("D_eligible$visits", datasources = conns)
#> $site
#> $site$class
#> [1] "integer"
#> 
#> $site$length
#> [1] 12
#> 
#> $site$`quantiles & mean`
#>   5%  10%  25%  50%  75%  90%  95% Mean 
#>    2    2    2    2    2    2    2    2

This aggregate describes the eligible episodes, not everybody in the database.

Make coverage explicit

An observation period states when the data source observes a person. The default requires exactly one period covering the index and drops missing or ambiguous coverage. A union policy can join adjacent periods when that matches the study.

covered <- eligible
covered$coverage <- omop_coverage(policy = "union", gap = 0)
coverage_recipe <- omop_recipe(populations = list(covered),
  outputs = omop_output("members", rows = "eligible", format = "membership"))
stopifnot(recipe_explain(coverage_recipe, conns = conns)$selected == "v2")
print(recipe_execute(coverage_recipe, out = c(members = "D_covered"), conns = conns))
#>     members 
#> "D_covered"

Here each person has one observation period, so the policy does not change membership. gap = 0 does not tolerate unobserved days. The earliest policy instead chooses one complete covering record; it does not union records. Coverage is not proof that a person took a drug or attended a visit.

Reuse an existing cohort

A results cohort is a named definition with private membership and start/end dates already available to the resource. Practice cohort 1 contains two of the four synthetic patterns. Its ID is a definition ID, not a patient ID.

cohort_population <- omop_population("saved", index = omop_index(
  list(cohort_definition_id = 1L), select = "all", end = omop_end("event_end")))
cohort_recipe <- omop_recipe(populations = list(cohort_population),
  outputs = omop_output("members", rows = "saved", format = "membership"))
stopifnot(recipe_explain(cohort_recipe, conns = conns)$selected == "v2")
print(recipe_execute(cohort_recipe, out = c(members = "D_cohort"), conns = conns))
#>    members 
#> "D_cohort"

This reads existing cohort episodes without writing a cohort to the database. Use omop_in_cohort(1L) as a criterion when you want membership alone while retaining a different index. Do not invent a cohort ID on a real resource.

Identify new users

A washout requires an observed period without the study exposure before entry. The shortcut combines drug records into eras, selects the first eligible era, and checks both observation and absence of prior exposure.

new_users <- omop_new_users(950001L, washout_days = 365, by = "concept")
new_user_recipe <- omop_study(new_users, outputs = "baseline",
  baseline = list(prior_fills = omop_count("drug_exposure", 950001L,
    window = omop_window(-365, -1))))
stopifnot(recipe_explain(new_user_recipe, conns = conns)$selected == "v2")
print(recipe_execute(new_user_recipe, out = c(baseline = "D_new_users"), conns = conns))
#>      baseline 
#> "D_new_users"

The synthetic medicine uses concept grouping explicitly; ingredient grouping is the normal default when the vocabulary supplies ingredient relationships. The era uses a 30-day gap and ends at the treatment interval end. “New user” means no recorded use during this washout, not no lifetime use.

dsBaseClient::ds.table("D_new_users$prior_fills", useNA = "no", datasources = conns)
#> $output.list
#> $output.list$TABLE_rvar.by.study_row.props
#>                        study
#> D_new_users$prior_fills site
#>                       0    1
#> 
#> $output.list$TABLE_rvar.by.study_col.props
#>                        study
#> D_new_users$prior_fills site
#>                       0    1
#> 
#> $output.list$TABLE_rvar.by.study_counts
#>                        study
#> D_new_users$prior_fills site
#>                       0   18
#> 
#> $output.list$TABLES.COMBINED_all.sources_proportions
#> D_new_users$prior_fills
#> 0 
#> 1 
#> 
#> $output.list$TABLES.COMBINED_all.sources_counts
#> D_new_users$prior_fills
#>  0 
#> 18 
#> 
#> 
#> $validity.message
#> [1] "Data in all studies were valid"

Zero prior fills is part of the inclusion definition, so this result is expected.

Define cases and the control pool

Risk-set sampling selects controls who are still eligible at each case’s event time. A person who becomes a case later may serve as a control earlier. For a compact teaching example the outcome is death.

outcome <- omop_event("death")
cases <- omop_population("cases", index = omop_index(outcome),
  filters = list(omop_observed(before = 365)))
controls <- omop_population("controls",
  filters = list(omop_observed(before = 365)))
class(cases)
#> [1] "omop_population" "list"

The control criteria are evaluated at the case’s date. The sampler also checks that a control is alive and has not had the outcome on or before that date.

Match at case time 

matched <- omop_population("matched", match = omop_match(
  cases = "cases", controls = "controls", outcome = outcome,
  match = list("calendar_year"), controls_per_case = 1L, seed = 42L,
  prior_outcome = "exclude", future_cases = "eligible",
  replacement = "between_sets", insufficient = "keep_available"))
class(matched)
#> [1] "omop_population" "list"

The seed fixes the sampling order. Controls may be reused between sets here; replacement = "none" forbids that reuse. If too few controls are available, this policy keeps those available; drop_case would discard that case’s set. Real studies may also match on sex, age bands or prior event strata.

matched_recipe <- omop_recipe(populations = list(cases, controls, matched),
  variables = list(is_case = omop_population_column("is_case"),
    weight = omop_population_column("sampling_weight")),
  outputs = omop_output("sample", rows = "matched", format = "wide"))
stopifnot(recipe_explain(matched_recipe, conns = conns)$selected == "v2")
print(recipe_execute(matched_recipe, out = c(sample = "D_matched"), conns = conns))
#>      sample 
#> "D_matched"

The match-set key stays protected on the server. Sampling weights and case status are available to approved downstream analyses.

dsBaseClient::ds.table("D_matched$is_case", useNA = "no", datasources = conns)
#> $output.list
#> $output.list$TABLE_rvar.by.study_row.props
#>                  study
#> D_matched$is_case site
#>                 0    1
#>                 1    1
#> 
#> $output.list$TABLE_rvar.by.study_col.props
#>                  study
#> D_matched$is_case site
#>                 0  0.5
#>                 1  0.5
#> 
#> $output.list$TABLE_rvar.by.study_counts
#>                  study
#> D_matched$is_case site
#>                 0   18
#>                 1   18
#> 
#> $output.list$TABLES.COMBINED_all.sources_proportions
#> D_matched$is_case
#>   0   1 
#> 0.5 0.5 
#> 
#> $output.list$TABLES.COMBINED_all.sources_counts
#> D_matched$is_case
#>  0  1 
#> 18 18 
#> 
#> 
#> $validity.message
#> [1] "Data in all studies were valid"

These are sampled rows, including repeated controls when permitted. They are not disease prevalence or counts of unique people. Matching defines a design; it does not by itself remove all confounding.

Recap

Index selection sets episodes; criteria and coverage decide eligibility. Existing cohorts, new-user eras and risk-set samples are population definitions in the same language.

Try it

Keep every visit episode instead of just the first, and inspect the resulting private membership schema.

Solution

all_visitors <- omop_population("visitors", index = omop_index(visits, select = "all"))
all_recipe <- omop_recipe(populations = list(all_visitors),
  outputs = omop_output("members", rows = "visitors", format = "membership"))
stopifnot(recipe_explain(all_recipe, conns = conns)$selected == "v2")
print(recipe_execute(all_recipe, out = c(members = "D_all_visitors"), conns = conns))
#>          members 
#> "D_all_visitors"
dsBaseClient::ds.colnames("D_all_visitors", datasources = conns)
#> $site
#> [1] "row_id"            "cohort_row_id"     "person_id"         "cohort_start_date"
#> [5] "cohort_end_date"   "index_source"

The keys distinguish episodes even when a person appears more than once. The synthetic verification harness checks 30 episodes for 18 distinct people.
